messages:
alex: Quick heads-up: I ran a simulation of three pseudonym strategies across 50k sample reqs: full-redact, partial-fuzzy (prefix+hash), and bucket-hash. Results attached in gist.
priya: can you summarise tradeoffs briefly?
alex: tl;dr: full-redact = lowest cardinality but bad for debugging. partial-fuzzy = preserves grouping but increases metric cardinality ~2.4x on some routes. bucket-hash = caps cardinality by hashing into N buckets, so tradeoff between utility and noise.
lucas: what's bucket-hash look like in config?
alex: example:
```
route: /v1/complete
pii_policy:
  mode: bucket_hash
  buckets: 256
  keep_prefix: 3
  hash: xxh128
  salt_kms_key: projects/prod/keys/tenant-k
n```
nina: interesting. with buckets=256, grouping is approximate but stable. Does that satisfy support when they need to trace a user flow?
alex: no, bucket_hashed ids are not reversible and only give coarse grouping. Support would need to escalate to a special unmask flow (if enabled) or use request-id linking.
priya: legal preference? non-reversible unless exceptional process?
nina: yes, Legal still prefers non-reversible for PII, but will allow reversible for exceptional cases if access is audited and requires SSO+ticket.
lucas: performance and telemetry cost notes?
alex: partial-fuzzy added ~0.5ms median; bucket-hash ~0.2ms. But partial-fuzzy made our metrics ingestion cost jump because cardinality expanded on chatty endpoints.
priya: can console show expected downstream cost before enabling? we should warn users.
nina: UX idea: preflight modal that shows estimated additional metric rows and estimated monthly ingestion cost delta. Button: Enable canary (10% traffic) / Cancel.
lucas: also need a safety net: auto-fallback if metric ingestion rate or cardinality crosses threshold. Who owns the policy? SRE?
priya: propose: default fallback owned by eng-platform; SRE can opt-in for auto-revert. config: fallback: {trigger: cardinality-increase:50pct, action: revert_to: redact, notify: #sre-oncall}.
alex: one more: schema versioning in logs. add header log_schema_v: "pii_v2" when pseudonymization applied. so downstream parsers can handle either v1 (redact) or v2.
nina: what about embeddings? we must not leak masked tokens into embedding service.
alex: policy: any field tagged pii_masked must be dropped before vectorization. We'll enforce in pipeline; rejects if tag present.
lucas: backfill problem: if we change strategy, historical logs have prior pseudonyms. Analytics might want to correlate across strategies. Any plan?
priya: recommended: keep historical salt + mapping for 90 days and provide a batch rehash tool for analytics teams if they request. But restrict to analytics role and log the action.
nina: add audit requirement to toggles. Console must require reason and ticket link when switching to a less-restrictive mode. record via audit-bot.
audit-bot: [auto] policy-change record at 1749992250 by alex: route=/v1/complete, from=redact, to=bucket_hash, buckets=256, scope=canary:team-beta
lucas: final question: revert path for suspected leak?
alex: runbook: 1) set global redact kill-switch (ops console) 2) suspend downstream sinks (analytics/embeddings) 3) rotate any salts if reversible keys used (via KMS) 4) notify legal + open incident ticket. Include this in RFC.
priya: can you draft RFC with perf numbers and console mockups? I'll loop in Legal and SRE for review.
nina: I'll prototype the preflight cost estimator next week.
alex: will open RFC and PR today. ping me for reviews.
audit-bot: [auto] thread archived at 1749992290 for compliance trace
